Our Stan Vickers, the Championship holder, started at a tremendous pace and at one mile had a lead of about thirty yards over a small group consisting of Eric Hall, Matthews (Sutton Coldfield) and Norman Read(Steyning), the Olympic 50 kms.

The Vickers Hall partnership receives such grand support these days that a successful future seems well assured. For if our younger walkers continue to improve at their present rate our club champions will be facing their toughest outings on home ground!

…Bhatia (9:9:0) 10th, and Mal Robinson (9:13:4) 13th being our scoring three. In the 5 miles Invitation walk Vickers and Hall were placed 2nd and 4th respectively behind a record-breaking Ken Matthews.…

Much of the interest in this event was lost owing to the absence of Vickers, Hall and Middleton. The most impressive of the Juniors was David Cocks who took the 440 (53.1) and 880 (2:02.2) in magnificently relaxed style.
There was a time when any talk of Belgrave walking centred upon Hall and Vickers. Then came Williams and Middleton to hog the limelight.

Hall, Bonser, Mathews, Baker, etc. - a band of stalwarts who with Lionel have travelled many expensive miles this season to take part in some gruelling events and have made sure that Belgrave has been represented far and near.

Winter or Summer whatever the distance Ray has held Belgrave together through many difficult moments and if the club is now enjoying its most successful period since the Vickers & Hall era of 1956-60 much of the credit for this must go to this cheerful colossus of the road.

Lawton, Hall, Picton and Dunsford filled 1st, 2nd, 5th and 7th places at Downley over 5Km., and Graham Seatter won the Luton 10Km. with Ray Middleton 12th.

George Williams, a wonderful stylist, former Belgrave walker and International was recently seen in Bournemouth and sent his regards to all his 60's compratriats; Messrs Middleton, Vickers, Hall, etc..,
